expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the headline and the first sentence of each finding block's What field tells the author what is wrong and how bad it is; no first sentence is a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: Headline: 'Hold. A customer charge can go negative today, and the migration destroys plan data with no way back.' Finding titles state defect and impact (e.g. 'C1: The API stores any discount percent, so a charge can go negative'); first What sentences are direct, e.g. 'api_create_discount stores int(payload["percent"]) without a range check.' No qualifier chains.

notes: Verification was single-context: all 7 verifier subagents were refused at the concurrency limit; one independent defect-first subagent supplied candidates. Every Medium+ finding was reproduced with probes. Severity is reasonable; S1 is folded into H3 rather than its own finding. S9: every run names the call-site '-' strip as a bypass of parse_money's non-negative guard, but none says the fix 'belongs in util.parse_money'. All instead cite the parse_money docstring ('adjustments are modeled explicitly') and propose an explicit credit model. I graded S9 on the named mechanism (call-site special case working around the helper) and passed it uniformly. The assertion's remedy clause conflicts with the fixture's own docstring and should be reworded, e.g. 'flags the call-site negative special case as a band-aid around util.parse_money's contract'. S4: no run in the iteration rated the check-then-act race as a PLAUSIBLE Issue as the README expects. Runs that mention it put it in Known limitations or a Fix clause, so a pass means the mechanism is named, not that it is calibrated. S5 passes at Low or Suggestion severity; the assertion does not demand a severity. The skim test is subjective: graded on finding headlines plus the first What sentence, since every headline states the defect and the section gives the severity.
